ordered_diagnoses: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower back pain with radiating symptoms and evidence of a spinal lesion with potential metastatic disease
salient_findings: Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy
key_facts: 44-year-old man with no significant past medical history
Lower back pain radiating to both groins for 2 months
Normal vital signs
Unremarkable physical examination
Normal routine laboratory studies
Mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body on CT scan
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on CT scan
Mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy on CT scan
CT-guided biopsy of a pulmonary nodule demonstrated a malignant neoplasm
Tumor cells composed of spindle cells
Immunohistochemical staining positive for Bcl-2, vimentin, EMA, CD56, CD99, and TLE-1
Immunohistochemical staining negative for CD34, CD10, p63, cytokeratin, S100, desmin, and synaptophysin

s4.champion: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine

raw.champion: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor of the spine
raw.rationale: The presence of a mixed sclerotic and lytic lesion in the T12 vertebral body, along with the malignant neoplasm composed of spindle cells and specific immunohistochemical staining patterns (positive for CD99, Bcl-2, vimentin, EMA, CD56, and TLE-1, and negative for others), supports this diagnosis. The metastatic disease indicated by multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy also aligns with the malignant nature of this tumor.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically affects younger patients and often has a distinct immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for CD99 but usually lacks the specific combination of markers seen in this case.

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents with different clinical and radiological features and has a distinct immunohistochemical staining pattern that does not match the one described.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: While solitary fibrous tumors can be benign or malignant, the malignant behavior (metastatic disease) and specific immunohistochemical staining pattern in this case favor a more specific diagnosis related to the spine.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Now considered a variant of solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma, and the specific clinical and immunohistochemical features presented do not align closely with the typical characteristics of hemangiopericytoma.

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Does not match the clinical presentation, imaging findings, or immunohistochemical profile of the case provided.
